dedupe_keys.name: cesm subgrid land surface climate projections

description: The Yale-led university research team deposits global CESM land-surface climate projections in Harvard Dataverse. The simulation covers 2015–2100 on a 0.9 by 1.25 degree grid under RCP8.5, separating urban, rural, tree, grass, shrub, bare-soil, crop and lake tiles. Variables describe physical state, energy fluxes, runoff and atmospheric forcing. NetCDF files and example analysis scripts are available free under CC0; the provider API confirms the published metadata even though the browser landing page did not render. Monthly and daily outputs cover the period, while hourly windows are limited to 2019–2023 and 2096–2100 and runoff is monthly. This is one model scenario, with known limitations in forest-versus-grass diurnal temperature responses. It can supply boundary conditions for urban heat, building-energy and water simulations. It complements data-cmip6-climate-projections-cds with explicit subgrid land-use contrasts.
